subject: Best way to add Y axis annotation (unit)

messages.author: 8c45483022d450d5
messages.subject: Best way to add Y axis annotation (unit)
parts:
Hi

I would like to add some metadata information concerning the unit of the Y axis, which would not be included in the ylab(). Ideally, it would come just above the last tick on the y axis, and would be specified without reference to the data/nature of the scale (i.e. data independant)

It seems this is quite complicated in ggplot2... what would you recommend for approach? I tried following:
-annotate() or geom_text(): does not seem appropriate since both can't plot outside the plot area, and use data specific scales
-scale_y_continuous() a possibility could be to add the last tick itself, like:
df<-data.frame(X=rnorm(100), Y=1:100)
qplot(x = X, y = Y, data = df) + scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0,100,20), labels = c(seq(0,80,20), "US $"))

this is quite nice, but however requires to remove one tick on the scale, and still is not data dependant (i.e. need to know which are the values to give in breaks and labels).
There would be maybe a trick to run the plot(), retrieve the infos on scale and just adapt, but I guess quite cumbersome since requires each plot to be computed twice?

- custom function: B Auguie submitted on this list a function to do something similar:
http://groups.google.com/group/ggplot2/browse_thread/thread/a5bd66677efc5610/618a606a6b2b6109?lnk=gst&q=unit+y+axis#618a606a6b2b6109

It is definitely nice, but quite scary to use it given the warning that this function will probably work only with simple plots and would likely fail with newer versions of ggplot2?

So I do not know exactly which way I should pursue... any ideas, advices?

Thanks!

mat

messages.author: 065110cca96a6373
messages.subject: Re: Best way to add Y axis annotation (unit)
parts:
Hi Matthieu,
 
My suggestion would be to use Baptiste's function.  Yes, it is not guaranteed to work with future versions of ggplot, but that's pretty much the case for all of R (or any software).  The good news, is that unless Hadley has some deep magic up his sleeve (and not that I would put it passed him, but my bet for a prior probability would be low), future versions of ggplot will continue using grid graphics, so Baptiste's function should be able to be edited with minimal effort to accomodate the new versions.  If you're interested, Paul Murrell (author of grid) published the second edition of R Graphics recently and it gives a very nice introduction to grid graphics.  I've recommended it to everyone who will give me the time of day :)  Finally got me using grid a bit, and I'm just a psychologist.
 
Cheers,
 
Josh
